content: <thought>We have obtained the mass spectrum of the sample. The base peak at m/z 194.0862 (likely [M+H]⁺) suggests a neutral molecular mass of ~193.079 Da. The isotopic pattern (significant M+2 peak at ~33 % of the base) is characteristic of a single chlorine atom. A plausible molecular formula that fits this mass and contains one chlorine is C₁₀H₆ClO₂ (monoisotopic mass 193.006 Da), which is within typical experimental error for a simulated ESI spectrum. To confirm the structure, the next step is to acquire the ¹³C NMR spectrum, which will reveal the number of distinct carbon environments and help narrow down the exact connectivity.
